U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show that about 63,700 molecular and cellular biologists were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 64,500 by 2034, a net increase of about 800 jobs, with roughly 4,800 openings per year and a median annual wage of about $93,300 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace molecular biologists, but it will reduce standard laboratory work. Automated experiments and high-throughput systems accelerate routine processes, shifting scientists from standard procedures toward experimental design, mechanistic interpretation, and research-direction decisions. People limited to standard procedures will lose ground, while those who can design studies and explain results will become more valuable.
